Why it fits / notes: Sister journal to Microbiome; explicitly welcomes all animal microbiome studies incl. non-model/wild species. Ideal home for a host-associated 16S study framed around holobiont/host effects.

Scope explicitly covers microbial community ecology, host–microbe interactions, phylogenetic/functional diversity and microbial evolutionary biology. Strong match for the ecological-context-dependence angle.
Long-standing venue for host-associated and environmental community ecology; comfortable with descriptive-but-hypothesis-driven field microbiome surveys.

Best fit conceptually for hybrid zones / introgression / speciation. BUT editors reject papers that are 'primarily descriptive and relevant only to the taxon studied' — would need the evolutionary/post-zygotic-isolation message sharpened and generalized to be competitive.
Microbial communities and interactions in the environment, including host-associated aquatic systems. Higher selectivity; fits if the environmental-gradient (anthropization) story is foregrounded.
Shorter-format sister journal to Env. Microbiol.; good landing spot for a focused regional result if Env. Microbiol. is too competitive.

Flagship for microbial ecology incl. ecological speciation (published comparable whitefish/stickleback work). A genuine stretch given sample size and descriptive scope — only if reframed with a strong mechanistic/conceptual advance.
Broad, sound-science ecology/evolution OA journal; explicitly the recommended home for solid taxon-focused studies not broad enough for Molecular Ecology.
Sound-science criterion (not novelty); strong track record for 16S microbiome ecology; moderate APC.
Large, fast, section on microbial symbioses/host-microbe systems; fits well thematically.
Broad evolutionary ecology OA venue; comfortable with hybrid-zone + microbiota framing.
Methodologically-judged megajournal; many cited papers here already; reliable fallback.
If reframed around fish biology/physiology rather than microbial evolutionary ecology.
Ecology of fishes incl. cyprinids; a specialized fit; lower reach.
